name: NY-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Lander's large fundraising edge over Moore
Open seat after Goldman lost renomination
model.rationale: This Brooklyn-based seat carries a D+32 lean, and Brad Lander has raised $2.45 million against Jennifer Moore's $2,700, while Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 98%. The open-seat status adds little risk in a district this blue.
model.watch: A surprise general-election polling error or an unexpectedly well-funded Republican outside campaign could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dan Goldman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
NY-10 is a heavily Democratic Brooklyn district, and incumbent Dan Goldman will not appear on the November ballot after losing renomination. City Comptroller Brad Lander enters the general as the Democratic nominee with a commanding financial position, having raised about $2.45 million, while Republican Jennifer Moore has raised under $3,000 and shows no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 98%, and the district's D+32 partisan lean leaves Republicans little realistic path. The forecast treats the seat as safely Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
